text:
Jordan Eberle is 36, the Kraken captain, and still the first name on their power play. Nine of his 16 points have come with the extra man, and on Nov. 25 he scored his 100th goal as a Kraken, a franchise milestone for a player who has been there since the expansion draft.

The production is real and sustainable in the narrow sense: eight goals on 7.1 expected, a shooting rate just above what our talent range expects, and his own chances at 1.12 expected goals per 60 minutes, identical to last season. The worry is at five on five. Seattle has only 42.5% of the expected goals with him on the ice, about four points worse than when he sits, and his ice time has drifted down to 16 minutes over the last ten games. He is also in the 11th percentile for top skating speed, which is what 36 looks like.

So the role is narrowing toward the power play and the net front, where he still scores. Watch whether his even-strength minutes keep sliding.
